sample_signals.customer_quote:
I am writing this review to caution fellow students and aspirants planning to study abroad about my experience with LeapScholar. While the platform presents itself as a one-stop solution for overseas education, the reality behind their operations is far from student-oriented. My journey with them has been not only disappointing but also financially and emotionally distressing.

The biggest issue lies in the fact that LeapScholar's system is purely target- and commission-driven. The counsellors do not prioritize what is genuinely beneficial for the student; instead, they focus on meeting internal targets and pushing students toward decisions that serve the platform’s commercial goals. This was evident in the misleading and factually incorrect information I was provided regarding university admission policies and visa processes.

Based on their advice, I made critical decisions and financial commitments—including application fees, documentation costs, and preparatory services—that ultimately went to waste due to the false and incomplete information given by their counsellors. When the situation turned adverse, LeapScholar completely distanced itself from any responsibility, offering neither support nor redressal for the loss I suffered.

Despite highlighting the losses I incurred—both in terms of time and a significant amount of money—there was no accountability or acknowledgment from their side. Their assurances were mostly oral and not backed by written communication, making it impossible to hold them accountable later.

It became clear that counsellors are pressured to meet sales targets, and many lack proper training or updated knowledge about international universities and their dynamic admission requirements. This kind of approach can seriously damage a student’s future and financial stability.

My strong advice to any student considering LeapScholar is this:
✅ Always verify every piece of information given to you with the official university sources.
✅ Never rely on oral promises—get everything in writing.
✅ Do not make any financial decisions based solely on their recommendations.
✅ Remember, you are investing not just money, but your future—choose your advisors wisely.

In summary, LeapScholar failed to provide accurate guidance, caused a significant financial loss, and did not take any responsibility when things went wrong. I hope my experience serves as a warning to others—be cautious, ask questions, and don’t fall into the trap of marketing-driven counselling.

sample_signals.customer_quote:
I had a very disappointing experience with LeapScholar.

Initially, the counselling process was quite good, and I was able to secure an offer letter from a university without much difficulty. I also received some support regarding my education loan, which was helpful.

However, the experience with the visa team was extremely frustrating. They seemed inexperienced and kept requesting additional documents at different stages—documents that could have been easily arranged earlier if they had guided me properly from the beginning. This lack of clarity and planning led to delays in my visa application.

It also felt like the team was unsure about the exact documentation requirements. Even after submitting everything, my visa was eventually rejected. Later, when I consulted other experts, I realized that my SOP could have been much more accurate and better structured, which might have improved my chances.

I do not wish to name any individual, but the overall service delivery and commitment need significant improvement.

Very disappointing experience. I would recommend others to consider alternative consultancies if they have better options available.

sample_signals.customer_quote:
LeapScholar was hands down one of the worst and most frustrating experiences I’ve ever had. They take a huge amount of money from students and in return provide absolutely useless classes, poor guidance, and zero real support.

The teachers are not helpful, the classes feel like a complete joke, and no one genuinely cares about your concerns once they’ve got your payment. Every time you have a doubt or need actual assistance, they either ignore you, delay things, or give no proper solution at all.

What’s most infuriating is how they sell big promises before enrollment, but once you’re in, you realize it’s all just pressure, false commitments, and disappointment. Instead of actually helping students, they seem more focused on forcing you into their classes and extracting as much money as possible.

This whole experience felt misleading, exploitative, and like a complete scam. I genuinely regret spending my money here. If you are thinking of joining, don’t make the same mistake. There are far better and more honest options out there.

sample_signals.customer_quote:
I requested a refund for Coursera Plus Subscription, but the process is extremely non-transparent. The system simply shows “Not eligible for refund” without providing any clear explanation, terms, or reasoning behind this decision. There is no visible link to detailed refund policy terms before purchase, and customer support does not proactively clarify the eligibility criteria.

This lack of transparency feels like a deliberate attempt to discourage refund requests rather than genuinely informing customers of their rights. Subscription-based platforms should clearly display refund eligibility conditions upfront — not bury them or leave customers guessing after the fact.

I would strongly recommend Coursera to make their refund policy more visible, accessible, and clearly communicated at the time of purchase. Until then, I’d advise potential subscribers to research third-party reviews before committing to Coursera Plus.
